contexts.text: Go in to my handmaid () = conjunction with what is exterior. AC 1902:2. AC 1909.
To go in = accession to doctrine, and recession from external things; but here the contrary.
This is signified by their entrance into Canaan.
I will go in to him, and will sup with him.
He who entereth not by the door.
On the first entrance of souls into the other life. SE 1742.
Ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered (). Explained.

By the things which enter into the mouth (), in the literal sense, is meant food of every kind... But in the spiritual sense there are meant all things which enter into the thought from the memory and also from the world... And those things which enter into the thought, and not at the same time into the will, do not render the man unclean... AE 580:3.
No one could enter into the temple (). (Explained.)
